questions.text: नीचे दिए गए किस विकल्प में मैग्नीशियम ऑक्साइड बनना सही दिखाया गया है?
questions.text_english: The formation of magnesium oxide is correctly shown in option:

options_english.A: Mg (2 electrons transferred to one O) → Mg²⁺ [O²⁻]
options_english.B: Mg (1 electron transferred to one O) → Mg⁺ [O⁻]
options_english.C: Mg (1 electron each transferred to two O atoms) → Mg²⁺ [O⁻]₂
options_english.D: 2Mg (1 electron each from two Mg to one O) → [Mg²⁺]₂ [O²⁻]

questions.image_description: Four diagrams showing electron dot structures and electron transfer between Mg and O atoms to form magnesium oxide. Option A shows Mg transferring 2 electrons to one O atom forming Mg²⁺ and O²⁻. Option B shows Mg transferring 1 electron to one O forming Mg⁺ and O⁻. Option C shows Mg transferring 1 electron each to two O atoms forming Mg²⁺ and [O⁻]₂. Option D shows 2 Mg atoms each transferring 1 electron to one O forming [Mg²⁺]₂ and O²⁻.
questions.solution: Option A is correct. Magnesium (Mg) has 2 valence electrons and oxygen (O) needs 2 electrons to complete its octet. Therefore, one Mg atom transfers both its valence electrons to a single O atom, forming Mg²⁺ and O²⁻ ions — this is the correct ionic bond in MgO. Option B is wrong because Mg cannot form Mg⁺ by losing only 1 electron as its second shell has 2 electrons. Option C incorrectly shows Mg²⁺ bonding with two O⁻ ions, giving MgO₂ which is not magnesium oxide. Option D incorrectly shows two Mg atoms each giving only 1 electron to one O, which does not satisfy the octet rule for Mg.
questions.solution_hindi: विकल्प A सही है। मैग्नीशियम (Mg) में 2 संयोजकता इलेक्ट्रॉन होते हैं और ऑक्सीजन को अष्टक पूर्ण करने के लिए 2 इलेक्ट्रॉन चाहिए। अतः एक Mg परमाणु अपने दोनों इलेक्ट्रॉन एक O परमाणु को देता है, जिससे Mg²⁺ और O²⁻ आयन बनते हैं — यह MgO में सही आयनिक बंध है।

questions.text: विद्युत-अपघटनी अपचयन प्रक्रिया द्वारा गलित क्लोराइडों से प्राप्त होने वाली धातुएँ हैं:
questions.text_english: The metals obtained from their molten chlorides by the process of electrolytic reduction are:

options.A: गोल्ड और सिल्वर / Gold and silver
options.B: कैल्शियम और मैग्नीशियम / Calcium and magnesium
options.C: ऐलुमिनियम और सिल्वर / Aluminium and silver
options.D: सोडियम और आयरन / Sodium and iron

questions.solution: Option B is correct. Calcium and magnesium are highly reactive metals that lie high up in the reactivity series. They cannot be extracted by reduction with carbon or by displacement reactions. Therefore, electrolytic reduction of their molten chlorides (CaCl₂ and MgCl₂) is used to obtain these metals. Gold and silver are low-reactivity metals found in free state or extracted by simple chemical reduction. Aluminium is extracted by electrolysis of molten alumina, not its chloride. Iron is extracted by reduction with coke in a blast furnace, not electrolysis.
questions.solution_hindi: विकल्प B सही है। कैल्शियम और मैग्नीशियम अत्यधिक अभिक्रियाशील धातुएँ हैं जो सक्रियता श्रेणी में ऊपर स्थित हैं। इन्हें कार्बन अपचयन द्वारा नहीं निकाला जा सकता, इसलिए इनके गलित क्लोराइडों के विद्युत-अपघटनी अपचयन से प्राप्त किया जाता है।

questions.text: लवण 'X' के एक सूत्र इकाई में क्रिस्टलन के जल के अणुओं की संख्या 7 है। लवण 'X' है:
questions.text_english: In one formula unit of salt 'X', seven molecules of water of crystallisation are present. The salt 'X' is:
questions.solution: Option C is correct. FeSO₄·7H₂O (ferrous sulphate heptahydrate), commonly known as green vitriol, contains 7 molecules of water of crystallisation per formula unit. CuSO₄·5H₂O (blue vitriol) has 5 water molecules. Na₂CO₃·10H₂O (washing soda) has 10 water molecules. CaSO₄·2H₂O (gypsum) has 2 water molecules. Therefore, the salt with 7 water molecules of crystallisation is FeSO₄.
questions.solution_hindi: विकल्प C सही है। FeSO₄·7H₂O (हरा कसीस) में प्रति सूत्र इकाई 7 क्रिस्टलन जल के अणु होते हैं। CuSO₄ में 5, Na₂CO₃ में 10 और CaSO₄ में 2 जल अणु होते हैं।

questions.text: दो तत्त्वों A और B के बीच अभिक्रिया से कोई यौगिक C बनता है। A इलेक्ट्रॉन खोता है तथा B इलेक्ट्रॉन ग्रहण करता है। यौगिक C निम्नलिखित में से कौन-सा एक गुण नहीं दर्शाएगा?
questions.text_english: Reaction between two elements A and B forms a compound C. A loses electrons and B gains electrons. Which one of the following properties will NOT be shown by compound C?

options.A: इसका गलनांक उच्च है। / It has high melting point.
options.B: यह जल में अत्यधिक विलेय है। / It is highly soluble in water.
options.C: इसके विजातीय (विपरीत आवेशित) आयनों के बीच दुर्बल स्थिर-वैद्युत आकर्षण बल है। / It has weak electrostatic forces of attraction between its oppositely charged ions.
options.D: यह अपनी गलित अवस्था अथवा जलीय विलयन में विद्युत चालन करता है। / It conducts electricity in its molten state or aqueous solution.

options_english.B: It is highly soluble in water.
options_english.C: It has weak electrostatic forces of attraction between its oppositely charged ions.
options_english.D: It conducts electricity in its molten state or aqueous solution.

questions.solution: Option C is correct — this is the property that compound C will NOT show. When A loses electrons and B gains electrons, an ionic compound C is formed. Ionic compounds are characterised by strong electrostatic forces of attraction between oppositely charged ions, NOT weak forces. Because of these strong forces, ionic compounds have high melting points (A is true), are generally soluble in water (B is true), and conduct electricity in molten state or aqueous solution (D is true). Therefore, the statement that ionic compounds have weak electrostatic forces is incorrect and this is the property they do not show.
questions.solution_hindi: विकल्प C सही है — यह वह गुण है जो यौगिक C नहीं दर्शाएगा। जब A इलेक्ट्रॉन खोता है और B ग्रहण करता है, तो आयनिक यौगिक C बनता है। आयनिक यौगिकों में विपरीत आवेशित आयनों के बीच प्रबल स्थिर-वैद्युत आकर्षण बल होता है, दुर्बल नहीं।

questions.text: जल का विद्युत-अपघटन एक वियोजन (अपघटन) अभिक्रिया है। जल के विद्युत-अपघटन के समय इलेक्ट्रोडों पर मुक्त गैसों – हाइड्रोजन और ऑक्सीजन के द्रव्यमानों का अनुपात (M_H : M_O) होता है:
questions.text_english: Electrolysis of water is a decomposition reaction. The mass ratio (M_H : M_O) of hydrogen and oxygen gases liberated at the electrodes during electrolysis of water is:
questions.solution: Option D is correct. The electrolysis of water produces hydrogen and oxygen in a volume ratio of 2:1 (H₂:O₂). The molecular mass of H₂ = 2 u and O₂ = 32 u. Mass of H₂ produced = 2 × 2 = 4 units and mass of O₂ = 1 × 32 = 32 units when 2 moles H₂ and 1 mole O₂ are formed. So M_H : M_O = 4 : 32 = 1 : 8. The volume ratio (2:1) should not be confused with the mass ratio (1:8).
questions.solution_hindi: विकल्प D सही है। जल के विद्युत-अपघटन में आयतन अनुपात H₂:O₂ = 2:1 होता है। H₂ का आण्विक द्रव्यमान 2 और O₂ का 32 है। अतः द्रव्यमान अनुपात = (2×2):(1×32) = 4:32 = 1:8।

questions.text:
निम्नलिखित अभिक्रियाओं पर विचार कीजिए:
(i) तनु हाइड्रोक्लोरिक अम्ल, सोडियम हाइड्रॉक्साइड से अभिक्रिया करता है।
(ii) मैग्नीशियम ऑक्साइड, तनु हाइड्रोक्लोरिक अम्ल से अभिक्रिया करता है।
(iii) कार्बन डाइऑक्साइड, सोडियम हाइड्रॉक्साइड से अभिक्रिया करती है।
यह पाया जाता है कि प्रत्येक प्रकरण में:
questions.text_english:
Consider the following reactions:
(i) Dilute hydrochloric acid reacts with sodium hydroxide.
(ii) Magnesium oxide reacts with dilute hydrochloric acid.
(iii) Carbon dioxide reacts with sodium hydroxide.
It is found that in each case:

options.A: लवण और जल बनता है। / Salt and water is formed.
options.B: उदासीन लवण बनते हैं। / Neutral salts are formed.
options.C: हाइड्रोजन गैस बनती है। / Hydrogen gas is formed.
options.D: अम्लीय लवण बनते हैं। / Acidic salts are formed.

questions.solution: Option A is correct. In all three reactions, a salt and water are formed. (i) HCl + NaOH → NaCl + H₂O; (ii) MgO + 2HCl → MgCl₂ + H₂O; (iii) CO₂ + 2NaOH → Na₂CO₃ + H₂O. Option B is wrong because reaction (iii) produces Na₂CO₃ which is a basic salt, not a neutral salt. Option C is wrong as no hydrogen gas is produced in any of these reactions. Option D is wrong as acidic salts are not formed in these reactions.
questions.solution_hindi: विकल्प A सही है। तीनों अभिक्रियाओं में लवण और जल बनते हैं। (i) HCl + NaOH → NaCl + H₂O; (ii) MgO + 2HCl → MgCl₂ + H₂O; (iii) CO₂ + 2NaOH → Na₂CO₃ + H₂O।

questions.text: वायु की उपस्थिति में ऐलुमिनियम और मैग्नीशियम के दहन होने पर बनने वाले उत्पाद क्रमशः हैं:
questions.text_english: The products formed when Aluminium and Magnesium are burnt in the presence of air respectively are:
questions.solution: Option B is correct. When aluminium burns in air, it forms aluminium oxide: 4Al + 3O₂ → 2Al₂O₃. When magnesium burns in air, it forms magnesium oxide: 2Mg + O₂ → 2MgO. Aluminium has a valency of 3 and oxygen has a valency of 2, giving the formula Al₂O₃. Magnesium has a valency of 2 and oxygen also has a valency of 2, giving the formula MgO. All other options contain incorrect chemical formulae.
questions.solution_hindi: विकल्प B सही है। ऐलुमिनियम के दहन से Al₂O₃ और मैग्नीशियम के दहन से MgO बनता है। Al की संयोजकता 3 और O की 2 होने से Al₂O₃ और Mg तथा O दोनों की संयोजकता 2 होने से MgO बनता है।

questions.text: वह कौन-सा पादप हॉर्मोन है जिसकी सांद्रता, प्ररोह के प्रकाश से दूर वाले भाग की कोशिकाओं को लम्बाई में वृद्धि के लिए उद्दीपित करती है?
questions.text_english: The plant hormone whose concentration stimulates the cells to grow longer on the side of the shoot which is away from light is:
questions.solution: Option D is correct. Auxin is the plant hormone responsible for phototropism. When light falls on one side of a shoot, auxin migrates to the shaded side (away from light). The higher concentration of auxin on the shaded side stimulates the cells there to elongate more, causing the shoot to bend towards the light source. Cytokinins promote cell division. Gibberellins promote stem elongation and seed germination. Adrenaline is an animal hormone, not a plant hormone.
questions.solution_hindi: विकल्प D सही है। ऑक्सिन पादप हॉर्मोन है जो प्रकाशानुवर्तन के लिए उत्तरदायी है। प्रकाश से दूर वाले भाग में ऑक्सिन की सांद्रता अधिक होती है जिससे वहाँ कोशिकाएँ अधिक लम्बी होती हैं और प्ररोह प्रकाश की ओर मुड़ जाता है।

questions.text: मुँह में लार का कम मात्रा में स्रावित होना किस परिवर्तन को प्रभावित करता है?
questions.text_english: Secretion of less saliva in mouth will affect the conversion of:

options.A: प्रोटीनों से ऐमीनो अम्ल / proteins into amino acids
options.B: वसा से वसीय अम्ल और ग्लिसरॉल / fats into fatty acids and glycerol
options.C: स्टार्च से सरल शर्करा / starch into simple sugars
options.D: शर्करा से ऐल्कोहॉल / sugars into alcohol

options_english.B: fats into fatty acids and glycerol

questions.solution: Option C is correct. Saliva contains the enzyme salivary amylase (ptyalin), which begins the digestion of starch in the mouth by breaking it down into simpler sugars like maltose. If less saliva is secreted, this initial digestion of starch will be affected. Proteins are digested by pepsin in the stomach. Fats are digested by lipase in the small intestine. Conversion of sugars to alcohol is a fermentation process carried out by yeast, not in the human digestive system.
questions.solution_hindi: विकल्प C सही है। लार में लाइसोज़ाइम और लार-एमिलेज (टायलिन) एंजाइम होता है जो मुँह में स्टार्च को सरल शर्करा (माल्टोज़) में तोड़ता है। लार कम होने पर यह प्रक्रिया प्रभावित होती है।

questions.text: गोल और हरे (RRyy) बीजों वाले मटर के पौधों का झुर्रीदार और पीले (rrYY) बीजों वाले मटर के पौधों के साथ संकरण कराया गया। F₁ संतति के पौधों द्वारा विकसित बीज होंगे:
questions.text_english: If pea plants with round and green seeds (RRyy) are crossed with pea plants having wrinkled and yellow seeds (rrYY), the seeds developed by the plants of F₁ generation will be:

options.A: 50% गोल और हरे / 50% round and green
options.B: 75% झुर्रीदार और हरे / 75% wrinkled and green
options.C: 100% गोल और पीले / 100% round and yellow
options.D: 75% झुर्रीदार और पीले / 75% wrinkled and yellow

questions.solution: Option C is correct. When RRyy (round, green) is crossed with rrYY (wrinkled, yellow), all F₁ offspring will have the genotype RrYy. Round (R) is dominant over wrinkled (r), and yellow (Y) is dominant over green (y). Therefore, all F₁ plants will express the dominant traits — round shape and yellow colour. Hence 100% of F₁ seeds will be round and yellow.
questions.solution_hindi: विकल्प C सही है। RRyy × rrYY संकरण से F₁ में सभी संतति RrYy होंगी। गोल (R) झुर्रीदार (r) पर और पीला (Y) हरे (y) पर प्रभावी है, इसलिए सभी F₁ बीज 100% गोल और पीले होंगे।

questions.text:
उभयलिंगी पुष्प के विषय में सही कथन है/हैं:
(i) इनमें पुंकेसर और स्त्रीकेसर दोनों होते हैं।
(ii) इनमें या तो पुंकेसर होता है अथवा स्त्रीकेसर होता है।
(iii) ये या तो स्वपरागण दर्शाते हैं अथवा परपरागण दर्शाते हैं।
(iv) ये अपने आप फल उत्पन्न नहीं कर सकते हैं।
questions.text_english:
The correct/true statement(s) for a bisexual flower is/are:
(i) They possess both stamen and pistil.
(ii) They possess either stamen or pistil.
(iii) They exhibit either self-pollination or cross-pollination.
(iv) They cannot produce fruits on their own.
questions.solution: Option C is correct. Statement (i) is true — a bisexual (hermaphrodite) flower contains both male (stamen) and female (pistil) reproductive organs. Statement (iii) is true — since a bisexual flower has both organs, it can undergo self-pollination (pollen from its own stamen falls on its stigma) or cross-pollination (pollen comes from another flower). Statement (ii) is false — that describes a unisexual flower. Statement (iv) is false — bisexual flowers can produce fruits on their own through self-pollination.
questions.solution_hindi: विकल्प C सही है। कथन (i) सत्य है — उभयलिंगी पुष्प में पुंकेसर और स्त्रीकेसर दोनों होते हैं। कथन (iii) सत्य है — इनमें स्वपरागण या परपरागण दोनों हो सकते हैं। कथन (ii) एकलिंगी पुष्प का वर्णन है और (iv) असत्य है।

questions.text:
निम्नलिखित ग्लूकोज़ के विखण्डन का पथ दर्शाया गया है:
ग्लूकोज़ →(a)→ पायरुवेट + ऊर्जा →(b)→ लैक्टिक अम्ल + ऊर्जा
स्थल 'a' और 'b' क्रमशः हैं:
questions.text_english:
The breakdown of glucose has taken the following pathway:
Glucose →(a)→ Pyruvate + Energy →(b)→ Lactic acid + Energy
The sites 'a' and 'b' respectively are:

options.A: माइटोकॉन्ड्रिया और ऑक्सीजन के अभाव वाली पेशीय कोशिकाएँ / Mitochondria and Oxygen deficient muscle cells
options.B: कोशिकाद्रव्य और ऑक्सीजन प्रचुर पेशीय कोशिकाएँ / Cytoplasm and Oxygen rich muscle cells
options.C: कोशिकाद्रव्य और यीस्ट कोशिकाएँ / Cytoplasm and Yeast cells
options.D: कोशिकाद्रव्य और ऑक्सीजन के अभाव वाली पेशीय कोशिकाएँ / Cytoplasm and Oxygen deficient muscle cells

options_english.A: Mitochondria and Oxygen deficient muscle cells
options_english.B: Cytoplasm and Oxygen rich muscle cells
options_english.D: Cytoplasm and Oxygen deficient muscle cells

questions.solution: Option D is correct. Glycolysis — the breakdown of glucose to pyruvate — occurs in the cytoplasm (cytosol) of all cells. This is site 'a'. The subsequent conversion of pyruvate to lactic acid occurs in oxygen-deficient (anaerobic) muscle cells during intense exercise when oxygen supply is insufficient. This is site 'b'. Note that pyruvate → ethanol + CO₂ occurs in yeast cells (anaerobic), and pyruvate → CO₂ + H₂O occurs in mitochondria (aerobic respiration).
questions.solution_hindi: विकल्प D सही है। ग्लूकोज़ का पायरुवेट में विखण्डन (ग्लाइकोलिसिस) कोशिकाद्रव्य में होता है — यह स्थल 'a' है। पायरुवेट से लैक्टिक अम्ल बनना ऑक्सीजन के अभाव वाली पेशीय कोशिकाओं में होता है — यह स्थल 'b' है।

questions.text: किसी काँच के प्रिज़्म में प्रवेश करता हुआ श्वेत प्रकाश अपने संघटक वर्णों में विभक्त हो जाता है। यह प्रेक्षण किया जाता है कि:
questions.text_english: The white light entering a glass prism, gets split into its constituent colours. It is observed that:

options.A: लाल प्रकाश सबसे अधिक विचलित होता है। / Red light deviates the most.
options.B: बैंगनी प्रकाश सबसे कम विचलित होता है। / Violet light deviates the least.
options.C: पीला प्रकाश नीले प्रकाश से अधिक विचलित होता है। / Yellow light deviates more than the blue light.
options.D: हरा प्रकाश नारंगी प्रकाश से अधिक विचलित होता है। / Green light deviates more than the orange light.

options_english.C: Yellow light deviates more than the blue light.
options_english.D: Green light deviates more than the orange light.

questions.solution: Option D is correct. The order of deviation in a prism from most to least is: Violet > Indigo > Blue > Green > Yellow > Orange > Red (VIBGYOR, reversed for deviation). Green light has a higher frequency than orange light, so it deviates more. Option A is wrong — violet deviates the most, not red. Option B is wrong — red deviates the least, not violet. Option C is wrong — blue deviates more than yellow, not the other way around.

questions.text_english: The percentage of solar energy which is NOT converted into food energy by the leaves of green plants in a terrestrial ecosystem is about:
questions.solution: Option D is correct. Green plants (producers) capture solar energy through photosynthesis. However, only about 1% of the solar energy incident on the leaves is actually converted into food energy (chemical energy stored in organic compounds). The remaining 99% is either reflected, transmitted, or used in transpiration and other processes. The question asks for the percentage NOT converted, which is 99%. The 10% law by Lindemann refers to energy transfer between trophic levels, not the efficiency of photosynthesis.

questions.text_english:

(i) Wolf, rabbit, grass, lion
(ii) Plankton, man, grasshopper, fish
(iii) Hawk, grass, snake, grasshopper, frog
(iv) Grass, snake, wolf, tiger
questions.solution: Option D is correct. A food chain must start with a producer (green plant/plankton) and follow a linear feeding sequence. Group (ii): Plankton → grasshopper → fish → man is not a valid chain because grasshoppers do not eat plankton and humans eat fish, not grasshoppers; the sequence is illogical. Group (iv): Grass → snake → wolf → tiger is invalid because snakes do not eat grass, and the sequence skips the herbivore level. Group (i) — Grass → rabbit → fox → lion is a valid chain. Group (iii) — Grass → grasshopper → frog → snake → hawk is a valid chain.

questions.text_english: "Excessive use of chemicals and pesticides in agriculture adversely affects the environment." Justify this statement.

key_points: Pesticides and chemicals enter food chains through the process of biological magnification (bioaccumulation).
They pollute soil and underground water, harming soil microorganisms and reducing soil fertility.

questions.solution: The excessive use of chemicals and pesticides in agriculture causes serious environmental damage through a process called biological magnification. Pesticides like DDT enter the food chain at the producer level and accumulate in increasing concentrations at higher trophic levels, ultimately causing harm to top consumers including humans. These chemicals also leach into the soil and seep into groundwater, making it unfit for drinking and killing beneficial soil microorganisms that maintain soil fertility. Additionally, pesticides destroy non-target organisms like bees, earthworms, and natural pest predators, thereby disturbing the ecological balance of the ecosystem.

questions.text_english:
(a) Consider the following circuits (i, ii, iii each with 5Ω resistors and 12V battery as shown):
In which circuit will the power dissipated in the circuit be (I) minimum (II) maximum? Justify your answer.
OR
(b) Two lamps, rated 100 W; 220 V and 60 W; 220 V are connected in parallel to electric main supply of 220 V. Find the current drawn by the two lamps from the supply.

key_points: (a) Power P = V²/R. Circuit (ii) has two 5Ω in series giving R=10Ω, so P = 144/10 = 14.4 W (minimum). Circuit (iii) has two 5Ω in parallel giving R=2.5Ω, so P = 144/2.5 = 57.6 W (maximum).
(b) Current drawn by 100W lamp = P/V = 100/220 A. Current drawn by 60W lamp = 60/220 A. Total current = (100+60)/220 = 160/220 = 8/11 ≈ 0.727 A.

questions.solution:
For part (a): Power dissipated P = V²/R. In circuit (i), one 5Ω resistor: P = (12)²/5 = 28.8 W. In circuit (ii), two 5Ω resistors in series: R = 10Ω, so P = 144/10 = 14.4 W (minimum). In circuit (iii), two 5Ω resistors in parallel: R = 2.5Ω, so P = 144/2.5 = 57.6 W (maximum). Higher resistance dissipates less power for the same voltage.

For part (b): In a parallel circuit, each lamp receives the full supply voltage of 220 V. Current through 100 W lamp = P/V = 100/220 A. Current through 60 W lamp = 60/220 A. Total current drawn = (100 + 60)/220 = 160/220 = 8/11 ≈ 0.73 A.

questions.text_english: An object is placed at a distance of 30 cm in front of a concave mirror of focal length 20 cm. Use mirror formula to determine the position of the image formed in this case.

key_points: Using mirror formula: 1/v + 1/u = 1/f. With u = -30 cm and f = -20 cm (concave mirror), 1/v = 1/f - 1/u = 1/(-20) - 1/(-30) = -1/20 + 1/30 = -3/60 + 2/60 = -1/60. Therefore v = -60 cm.
The image is formed at 60 cm in front of the mirror (on the same side as the object), and is real and inverted.

questions.solution: Using the mirror formula: 1/v + 1/u = 1/f. Applying the sign convention, object distance u = -30 cm (object in front of mirror) and focal length f = -20 cm (concave mirror). Therefore, 1/v = 1/f - 1/u = 1/(-20) - 1/(-30) = -1/20 + 1/30 = (-3 + 2)/60 = -1/60. So v = -60 cm. The negative sign indicates that the image is formed 60 cm in front of the concave mirror, on the same side as the object. The image is real and inverted.
questions.solution_hindi: दर्पण सूत्र: 1/v + 1/u = 1/f। चिह्न परिपाटी से u = -30 cm और f = -20 cm। 1/v = -1/20 + 1/30 = -3/60 + 2/60 = -1/60, अतः v = -60 cm। प्रतिबिम्ब दर्पण के सामने 60 cm की दूरी पर वास्तविक और उलटा बनता है।

questions.text:

अथवा
(ख) (i) पादपों की वहन तंत्र प्रणाली जन्तुओं की अपेक्षा धीमी होती है। कारण दीजिए।
(ii) पादपों में पदार्थों के स्थानान्तरण/परिवहन में फ़्लोएम की भूमिका का उल्लेख कीजिए।
questions.text_english:
(a) Besides minimising the loss of blood, why is it essential to plug any leak in a blood vessel? Name the component of blood which helps in this process and state how this component performs this function.
OR
(b) (i) The transport system in plants is relatively slower than in animals. Give reasons.
(ii) State the role of phloem in the transport of materials in plants.

key_points: (a) Besides blood loss, an open wound allows entry of microorganisms/pathogens, leading to infection. Platelets (thrombocytes) help plug the leak. They clump together at the site of injury and release chemicals that help form a fibrin clot (thrombus), sealing the wound.

(b)(i) Plants lack a pumping organ like the heart; transport depends on osmosis, diffusion, and transpiration pull which are much slower. (ii) Phloem transports food (sucrose and amino acids) prepared by leaves to all parts of the plant through a process called translocation, using energy (ATP).

questions.solution:
For part (a): Besides minimising blood loss, it is essential to plug leaks in blood vessels to prevent entry of microorganisms and pathogens from the environment, which could cause serious infections. Platelets (thrombocytes) are the blood component responsible for this. When a blood vessel is damaged, platelets aggregate at the injury site and release chemical signals that convert fibrinogen into fibrin, forming a mesh-like clot that seals the wound and prevents further bleeding and infection.

For part (b)(i): The transport system in plants is slower because plants do not have a muscular pumping organ like the heart. Transport depends on passive processes like osmosis, diffusion, and transpiration pull, which operate at a much slower rate. (ii) Phloem is responsible for translocation — the transport of photosynthetically prepared food (mainly sucrose) and other organic substances from leaves to all other parts of the plant including roots, using energy in the form of ATP.
questions.solution_hindi:
भाग (क): रक्त हानि के अलावा, वाहिनी में रिसाव रोकना इसलिए भी आवश्यक है ताकि पर्यावरण से रोगाणुओं का प्रवेश न हो। बिम्बाणु (Platelets) इस प्रक्रिया में सहायक हैं — ये घाव पर एकत्र होकर फाइब्रिन थक्का बनाते हैं।
भाग (ख)(i): पादपों में हृदय जैसा पम्पिंग अंग नहीं होता; परिवहन परासरण, विसरण और वाष्पोत्सर्जन खिंचाव पर निर्भर करता है। (ii) फ्लोएम ATP ऊर्जा का उपयोग करके पत्तियों में बने भोजन (सुक्रोज़) को पौधे के सभी भागों में स्थानांतरित करता है।

questions.text_english: Draw labelled diagrams to show different stages of budding in Hydra.

key_points: Diagram showing three stages: (1) Parent Hydra with a small outgrowth/bud forming on the body wall, (2) Bud grows larger and develops tentacles, (3) Fully formed young Hydra detaches from parent body.
Labels must include: Parent Hydra, Bud, Tentacles, Young Hydra.

questions.solution: Budding in Hydra proceeds through three main stages. In Stage 1, a small outgrowth called a bud develops on the body wall of the parent Hydra due to repeated cell division. In Stage 2, the bud gradually grows larger and develops its own tentacles while still attached to the parent body. In Stage 3, the fully developed young Hydra separates from the parent body and becomes an independent organism. The diagram should show all three stages clearly labelled with: Parent Hydra, Bud, Tentacles of bud, and Young/Daughter Hydra detaching.

questions.text_english:
What happens when: (write balanced chemical equation)
(a) Lead nitrate is thermally decomposed,
(b) Natural gas burns in oxygen (or air)?

key_points: (a) 2Pb(NO₃)₂ → (heat) → 2PbO + 4NO₂ + O₂. Yellow fumes of NO₂ are released and lead monoxide (yellow solid) is formed.
(b) CH₄ + 2O₂ → CO₂ + 2H₂O. Natural gas (methane) burns completely in oxygen to produce carbon dioxide and water.

questions.solution:
For part (a): When lead nitrate is thermally decomposed (heated strongly), it decomposes to form lead monoxide, nitrogen dioxide gas (brown fumes), and oxygen gas. The balanced equation is: 2Pb(NO₃)₂ → (heat) → 2PbO + 4NO₂ + O₂. Brown/yellow fumes of NO₂ are observed during this reaction.

For part (b): Natural gas is mainly methane (CH₄). When it burns completely in oxygen or air, carbon dioxide and water vapour are produced. The balanced equation is: CH₄ + 2O₂ → CO₂ + 2H₂O. This is a combustion reaction and is highly exothermic.

(ख) 0·01 cm त्रिज्या के किसी तार का प्रतिरोध 14 Ω है। यदि तार के पदार्थ की प्रतिरोधकता 44 × 10⁻⁸ Ωm है, तो तार की लम्बाई ज्ञात कीजिए। (दिया गया है π = 22/7)
questions.text_english:
(a) Define one ampere.
(b) The resistance of a wire of 0·01 cm radius is 14 Ω. If the resistivity of the material of the wire is 44 × 10⁻⁸ Ωm, find the length of the wire. (Given π = 22/7)

key_points: One ampere is defined as that amount of electric current which flows through a conductor when a charge of one coulomb passes through it in one second. (1A = 1C/1s)

questions.solution:
Part (a): One ampere is defined as that steady electric current which flows through a conductor when one coulomb of electric charge passes through a cross-section of it in one second. Mathematically, 1 A = 1 C / 1 s.

Part (b): Given — Radius r = 0.01 cm = 0.01 × 10⁻² m = 10⁻⁴ m; Resistance R = 14 Ω; Resistivity ρ = 44 × 10⁻⁸ Ωm. Cross-sectional area A = πr² = (22/7) × (10⁻⁴)² = (22/7) × 10⁻⁸ m². Using the formula R = ρL/A, we get L = RA/ρ = 14 × [(22/7) × 10⁻⁸] / [44 × 10⁻⁸] = 14 × 22 / (7 × 44) = 308/308 = 1 m. Therefore, the length of the wire is 1 m.
questions.solution_hindi:
भाग (क): एक ऐम्पियर वह विद्युत धारा है जब किसी चालक से 1 सेकण्ड में 1 कूलॉम आवेश प्रवाहित हो।
भाग (ख): r = 10⁻⁴ m, A = πr² = (22/7) × 10⁻⁸ m², L = RA/ρ = 14 × (22/7) × 10⁻⁸ / (44 × 10⁻⁸) = 1 m।
questions.topic: Electric current definition, Resistivity, Length of wire calculation

questions.text: किसी उत्तल दर्पण द्वारा बनने वाले प्रतिबिम्ब की प्रकृति, स्थिति और सापेक्ष साइज़ को दर्शाने के लिए उस प्रकरण में किरण आरेख खींचिए जिसमें बिम्ब (i) अनन्त पर स्थित है तथा (ii) दर्पण के ध्रुव P और अनन्त के बीच स्थित है।
questions.text_english: Draw ray diagrams to show the nature, position and relative size of the image formed by a convex mirror when the object is placed (i) at infinity and (ii) between infinity and pole P of the mirror.

key_points: (i) Object at infinity: Rays parallel to principal axis, reflected rays appear to diverge from focus F behind mirror. Image is at focus F, virtual, erect and highly diminished (point-sized).

(ii) Object between P and infinity: Two rays — one parallel to principal axis reflects as if from focus, one directed towards centre of curvature reflects back along same path. Image formed between P and F, virtual, erect and diminished.

questions.solution:
For a convex mirror, both cases produce virtual, erect and diminished images.

Case (i) — Object at infinity: Incident rays parallel to the principal axis fall on the convex mirror and after reflection appear to diverge from the principal focus F (located behind the mirror). The image is formed at the focus F, is virtual, erect and highly diminished (almost point-sized). The ray diagram must show parallel rays striking the mirror and the reflected rays diverging, with their extensions meeting at F behind the mirror.

Case (ii) — Object between P and infinity: Using standard rays, the image is formed between the pole P and focus F, behind the mirror. It is virtual, erect and diminished. As the object moves from infinity towards the pole, the image also moves from focus F towards the pole, always remaining smaller than the object.

(i) अनन्त पर बिम्ब: मुख्य अक्ष के समांतर किरणें परावर्तन के बाद फोकस F (दर्पण के पीछे) से आती प्रतीत होती हैं। प्रतिबिम्ब F पर, आभासी, सीधा, अत्यंत छोटा।
(ii) P और अनन्त के बीच बिम्ब: प्रतिबिम्ब P और F के बीच, आभासी, सीधा, छोटा।

अथवा
(ख) (i) उन दो धातुओं के नाम लिखिए जो ठंडे जल के साथ तीक्ष्णता से अभिक्रिया करती हैं। उन तीन प्रेक्षणों की सूची बनाइए जिन्हें कोई छात्र इन धातुओं को जल से भरे बीकर में डालने पर नोट करेगा।
(ii) इन धातुओं की जल के साथ अभिक्रिया में निकलने वाली गैस (यदि कोई हो) की पहचान के लिए कोई परीक्षण लिखिए।
questions.text_english:
(a) With the help of an activity, explain the conditions under which iron articles get rusted.
OR
(b) (i) Name two metals which react violently with cold water. List any three observations which a student notes when these metals are dropped in a beaker containing water.
(ii) Write a test to identify the gas evolved (if any) during the reaction of these metals with water.

key_points: (a) Activity: Three test tubes — (1) iron nail in plain water (rusts), (2) iron nail in boiled/oil-sealed water without air (no rust), (3) iron nail in dry air using CaCl₂ without water (no rust). Conclusion: Both water and oxygen (air) are necessary for rusting.

(b)(i) Sodium (Na) and Potassium (K). Observations: metal floats and moves vigorously, fizzing/bubbling occurs, metal melts to a ball/catches fire (K burns with lilac flame), heat is generated, the solution turns alkaline (turns litmus red to blue).
(b)(ii) Test: Collect the gas in an inverted test tube and bring a burning matchstick near its mouth — if it burns with a 'pop' sound, the gas is hydrogen (H₂).

questions.solution:
For part (a): Take three test tubes. In the first, place an iron nail in water open to air — rust forms on the nail. In the second, place a nail in boiled water sealed with oil (no dissolved oxygen) — no rust forms. In the third, place a nail in dry air using anhydrous calcium chloride (no moisture) — no rust forms. This activity proves that both water (moisture) and oxygen (from air) are simultaneously required for rusting of iron. Chemically: 4Fe + 3O₂ + 6H₂O → 4Fe(OH)₃ → Fe₂O₃·xH₂O (rust).

For part (b)(i): Sodium (Na) and Potassium (K) react violently with cold water. Observations: (1) The metal pieces float and dart about rapidly on the water surface. (2) Vigorous bubbling/fizzing occurs due to gas evolution. (3) The metal melts into a ball; potassium catches fire with a lilac/violet flame. (b)(ii) To identify the gas, collect it in an inverted test tube. When a burning splint/matchstick is brought near the mouth of the tube, a characteristic 'pop' sound confirms the presence of hydrogen gas.
questions.solution_hindi:
भाग (क): तीन परखनलियों में — (1) लोहे की कील जल और वायु में (जंग लगती है), (2) उबले जल में तेल से बंद (जंग नहीं), (3) शुष्क वायु में (जंग नहीं)। निष्कर्ष: जंग के लिए जल और ऑक्सीजन दोनों आवश्यक हैं।
भाग (ख)(i): सोडियम और पोटैशियम। प्रेक्षण: धातु तेजी से तैरती है, बुलबुले निकलते हैं, K में बैंगनी ज्वाला।
(ii) परखनली में गैस एकत्र करें; जलती तीली लाने पर 'पॉप' की आवाज़ आए तो गैस हाइड्रोजन है।

questions.text:
(क) "सक्रियता श्रेणी में मध्य की धातुओं के निष्कर्षण में भी विस्थापन अभिक्रियाओं की मुख्य भूमिका होती है।" दो उदाहरण देकर इस कथन की पुष्टि कीजिए।
(ख) सक्रियता श्रेणी में सबसे ऊपर स्थित धातुओं को उनके ऑक्साइडों को कार्बन द्वारा अपचयित करके प्राप्त क्यों नहीं किया जा सकता है?
questions.text_english:
(a) "Displacement reactions also play a key role in extracting metals in the middle of the reactivity series." Justify this statement with two examples.
(b) Why can metals high up in the reactivity series not be obtained by reduction of their oxides by carbon?

key_points: (a) Example 1: Iron is extracted using coke (carbon) in a blast furnace by carbon reduction — Fe₂O₃ + 3C → 2Fe + 3CO (though thermite, not typical displacement in simple sense). Better example: Copper is displaced by iron — Fe + CuSO₄ → FeSO₄ + Cu. Zinc: ZnO + C → Zn + CO.
(a) Example 2: Copper from copper sulphate solution by iron: Fe + CuSO₄ → FeSO₄ + Cu. This is used to recover copper from waste solutions.

(b) Metals high in the reactivity series (Na, K, Ca, Mg, Al) are very strong reducing agents. Carbon is not a stronger reducing agent than these metals, so it cannot reduce their oxides. Furthermore, the high temperatures required would also lead to other unwanted reactions. Therefore, electrolytic reduction is used instead.

questions.solution:
Part (a): Displacement reactions are crucial in extracting middle-activity metals. Example 1 — Iron is extracted from its oxide in a blast furnace where coke (carbon) displaces iron: Fe₂O₃ + 3C → 2Fe + 3CO₂. Carbon acts as a reducing agent displacing iron from its oxide. Example 2 — Copper can be recovered from copper sulphate solution by adding scrap iron: Fe + CuSO₄ → FeSO₄ + Cu. Here, more reactive iron displaces less reactive copper from its salt solution, demonstrating displacement.

Part (b): Metals that are very high in the reactivity series, such as sodium, potassium, calcium, magnesium and aluminium, are extremely powerful reducing agents. Carbon (coke) is not reactive enough to reduce their oxides because these metals have a greater affinity for oxygen than carbon does. Since carbon cannot form more stable oxides than these metals' oxides under practical conditions, it fails to displace them. Therefore, electrolytic reduction of their molten ores is the only feasible method.

मेंडल के किसी एक प्रयोग में जब गोल और पीले बीज वाले F₁ पीढ़ी के मटर के पौधों का स्वपरागण कराया गया, तो F₂ पीढ़ी में निम्नलिखित संयोजनों के मटर के बीज प्राप्त हुए:
बीज — गोल पीले: 800, गोल हरे: 275, झुर्रीदार पीले: 268, झुर्रीदार हरे: 90
इस परिणाम का विश्लेषण कीजिए और लक्षणों की आनुवंशिकता की उस क्रियाविधि का वर्णन कीजिए जो उपर्युक्त परिणामों की व्याख्या करती है।
questions.text_english:
In one of Mendelian experiments, when F₁ generation pea plants with round yellow seeds were self-pollinated, pea seeds with the following combinations were obtained in F₂ generation:
Seeds — Round yellow: 800, Round green: 275, Wrinkled yellow: 268, Wrinkled green: 90
Analyse the result and describe the mechanism of inheritance of traits which explains the above results.

key_points: The ratio 800:275:268:90 approximates 9:3:3:1, which is the expected ratio in a dihybrid cross F₂ generation.
This demonstrates Mendel's Law of Independent Assortment — two pairs of contrasting traits are inherited independently of each other.
F₁ plants are RrYy; upon self-pollination they produce gametes RY, Ry, rY, ry in equal proportions; combining gives 9 round yellow : 3 round green : 3 wrinkled yellow : 1 wrinkled green.

questions.solution:
The results show four phenotypic classes in the ratio 800:275:268:90, which approximately equals 9:3:3:1. This is the characteristic phenotypic ratio observed in the F₂ generation of a dihybrid cross, demonstrating Mendel's Law of Independent Assortment.

The F₁ plants had genotype RrYy (round = dominant R, yellow = dominant Y). Upon self-pollination, each F₁ plant produces four types of gametes in equal proportion: RY, Ry, rY, and ry. When these gametes combine randomly (16 possible combinations), they produce the 9:3:3:1 ratio — 9 round yellow (R_Y_) : 3 round green (R_yy) : 3 wrinkled yellow (rrY_) : 1 wrinkled green (rryy). This proves that the genes for seed shape and seed colour are located on separate chromosomes and assort independently during gamete formation.
questions.solution_hindi: परिणाम 800:275:268:90 ≈ 9:3:3:1 अनुपात दर्शाते हैं। यह द्विसंकर क्रॉस का F₂ अनुपात है। F₁ पौधे RrYy थे। स्वपरागण पर RY, Ry, rY, ry युग्मक बनते हैं जो संयोजित होकर 9 गोल पीले : 3 गोल हरे : 3 झुर्रीदार पीले : 1 झुर्रीदार हरे देते हैं। यह मेंडल के स्वतंत्र अपव्यूहन के नियम को प्रमाणित करता है।

questions.text_english:
(a) Name the glands that secrete:
(i) Adrenaline
(ii) Thyroxin
(b) Explain with example how the timing and amount of hormone released are regulated in the human body.

key_points: (a)(i) Adrenaline is secreted by the adrenal glands (located above the kidneys). (ii) Thyroxin is secreted by the thyroid gland (located in the neck).

(b) Hormone regulation occurs through feedback mechanisms. Example: Thyroid hormone regulation — when blood thyroxine level is low, the hypothalamus releases TRH which signals the pituitary to release TSH, which then stimulates the thyroid to produce thyroxine. When thyroxine levels rise to normal, it inhibits further TSH secretion (negative feedback loop).

questions.solution:
Part (a): (i) Adrenaline (also called epinephrine) is secreted by the adrenal glands, which are located on top of each kidney. (ii) Thyroxin is secreted by the thyroid gland, located in the neck region around the trachea.

Part (b): The timing and amount of hormones in the human body are controlled by a feedback mechanism. Example — regulation of thyroxin from the thyroid gland: When the level of thyroxin in the blood falls below normal, the hypothalamus (in the brain) detects this and releases thyroid-releasing hormone (TRH), which signals the pituitary gland to secrete thyroid-stimulating hormone (TSH). TSH then stimulates the thyroid gland to produce more thyroxin. When thyroxin levels rise back to normal, it sends an inhibitory signal to the pituitary and hypothalamus to stop releasing TSH — this is called negative feedback regulation. This mechanism ensures hormones are released in appropriate amounts at the right time.
questions.solution_hindi:

(क) (i) किसी लेंस 'X' की क्षमता – 2·5 D है। इस लेंस का नाम लिखिए और इसकी फोकस दूरी cm में निर्धारित कीजिए। नेत्र चिकित्सक किस दृष्टि दोष के संशोधन के लिए इस प्रकार के लेंस को संशोधक लेंस के रूप में निर्धारित करते हैं?
(ii) "किसी लेंस के लिए आवर्धन 'm' का मान – 2 है।" नई कार्तीय चिह्न परिपाटी का उपयोग करते हुए और यह मानते हुए कि कोई बिम्ब इस लेंस के प्रकाशिक केन्द्र से 20 cm की दूरी पर है, निम्नलिखित का उल्लेख कीजिए: (I) बनने वाले प्रतिबिम्ब की प्रकृति; (II) बिम्ब के साइज़ की तुलना में प्रतिबिम्ब का साइज़; (III) प्रतिबिम्ब की स्थिति, तथा (IV) प्रतिबिम्ब की ऊँचाई का चिह्न।

(ख) (i) किसी काँच के आयताकार स्लैब से प्रकाश की किसी किरण का अपवर्तन होना दर्शाने के लिए किरण आरेख खींचिए जबकि प्रकाश किरण वायु से काँच में तिरछी आपतन कर रही है।

questions.text_english:
(a) (i) The power of a lens 'X' is – 2·5 D. Name the lens and determine its focal length in cm. For which eye defect of vision will an optician prescribe this type of lens as a corrective lens?
(ii) 'The value of magnification m for a lens is –2.' Using new Cartesian Sign Convention and considering that an object is placed at a distance of 20 cm from the optical centre of this lens, state: (I) the nature of the image formed; (II) size of the image compared to the size of the object; (III) position of the image, and (IV) sign of the height of the image.
(iii) The numerical values of the focal lengths of two lenses A and B are 10 cm and 20 cm respectively. Which one of the two will show higher degree of convergence/divergence? Give reason to justify your answer.
OR
(b) (i) Draw a ray diagram to show the refraction of a ray of light through a rectangular glass slab when it falls obliquely from air into glass.
(ii) State Snell's law of refraction of light.
(iii) Differentiate between the virtual images formed by a convex lens and a concave lens on the basis of: (I) object distance, and (II) magnification.

key_points: (a)(i) Negative power (-2.5D) indicates concave lens. f = 1/P = 1/(-2.5) = -0.4 m = -40 cm. Used to correct myopia (short-sightedness).

(a)(ii) m = -2, object at u = -20 cm. v = m × u = (-2) × (-20) = 40 cm (positive). Nature: real and inverted; Size: twice the object; Position: 40 cm on the other side of lens; Height sign: negative (inverted).
(a)(iii) Lens A (f=10cm) has higher power P=1/0.1=10D than Lens B (f=20cm) P=5D. Higher power means higher degree of convergence/divergence. So Lens A.

(b)(i) Ray diagram showing incident ray, refracted ray inside glass slab, emergent ray parallel to incident ray but laterally displaced. (ii) Snell's law: sin i / sin r = constant = n (refractive index). (iii) Convex lens: virtual image when object is between O and F (object distance < focal length), magnification >1. Concave lens: virtual image for all object positions, magnification <1 always.

questions.solution:
Part (a)(i): Negative power of –2.5 D indicates that lens X is a concave (diverging) lens. Focal length f = 1/P = 1/(–2.5) = –0.4 m = –40 cm. An optician prescribes a concave lens to correct myopia (near-sightedness or short-sightedness), a condition in which the image of a distant object is formed in front of the retina.

Part (a)(ii): Magnification m = –2 (negative sign indicates real, inverted image). Object distance u = –20 cm (by sign convention). Since m = v/u, we get v = m × u = (–2) × (–20) = +40 cm. Conclusions: (I) The image is real and inverted. (II) The image is twice the size of the object (|m| = 2). (III) The image is positioned 40 cm on the other side of the lens (positive v means image is on the opposite side from the object). (IV) Since the image is inverted, the height of the image is negative.

Part (a)(iii): Lens A with focal length 10 cm has power P_A = 1/0.10 = 10 D, and Lens B with focal length 20 cm has power P_B = 1/0.20 = 5 D. Since power represents the ability to converge or diverge light, Lens A with higher power (10 D) shows a higher degree of convergence or divergence compared to Lens B.

OR Part (b)(i): The ray diagram shows an incident ray hitting the top surface of the glass slab at an angle of incidence i, refracting into the glass at angle r (r < i since glass is denser). The ray travels through the glass and hits the bottom surface, emerging as a ray parallel to the original incident ray but displaced laterally — this is called lateral displacement. (ii) Snell's law: The ratio of the sine of the angle of incidence to the sine of the angle of refraction is constant for a given pair of media: sin i / sin r = n₂/n₁. (iii) Convex lens forms a virtual image only when the object is placed between the optical centre and the focus (object distance < focal length); the magnification is greater than 1 (image is magnified). Concave lens always forms a virtual image regardless of the position of the object; the magnification is always less than 1 (image is diminished).

(ii): m = –2, u = –20 cm, v = 40 cm। प्रतिबिम्ब वास्तविक, उलटा, दोगुना बड़ा, लेंस के दूसरी ओर 40 cm पर। ऊँचाई का चिह्न ऋणात्मक।

questions.text_english:
(a) A saturated organic compound 'A' with two carbon atoms belongs to the homologous series of alcohols. On oxidation, it forms an organic acid 'B' with molecular mass 60 u. On heating 'A' with excess concentrated sulphuric acid at 443 K, an unsaturated hydrocarbon 'C' is formed.
(i) Name A, B and C.
(ii) Calculate molecular mass of C.
(iii) What happens when a pinch of sodium carbonate is added to compound B? Write chemical equation for the reaction.
(iv) Draw electron dot structure of compound B.
OR
(b) (i) What is a homologous series of carbon compounds? Write the name and formula of three successive members of the homologous series of compounds having functional group –COOH.
(ii) Write the name of two carbon compounds in which carbon atoms are arranged in the form of a ring. Draw the structure of any one of the two.

key_points: (a)(i) A = Ethanol (C₂H₅OH); B = Acetic acid/Ethanoic acid (CH₃COOH, mol. mass = 60u); C = Ethene (C₂H₄).
(ii) Molecular mass of C (ethene, CH₂=CH₂) = 2×12 + 4×1 = 28 u.
(iii) CO₂ gas is evolved with effervescence. 2CH₃COOH + Na₂CO₃ → 2CH₃COONa + H₂O + CO₂.
(iv) Electron dot structure of CH₃COOH showing all bonds: C-H, C-C, C=O and O-H with lone pairs on oxygen atoms.
(b)(i) Homologous series: successive members differ by –CH₂– (14u). Carboxylic acid series: Methanoic acid (HCOOH), Ethanoic acid (CH₃COOH), Propanoic acid (C₂H₅COOH).
(b)(ii) Benzene (C₆H₆) and Cyclohexane (C₆H₁₂). Structure of benzene shows a hexagonal ring with alternating double bonds.

questions.solution:
Part (a)(i): Compound A is a saturated alcohol with 2 carbon atoms — this is Ethanol (C₂H₅OH). On oxidation, ethanol forms acetic acid (ethanoic acid, CH₃COOH) which has molecular mass = 12+3+1+12+16+16+1 = 60 u — this is compound B. When ethanol is heated with excess concentrated H₂SO₄ at 443 K (dehydration), water is eliminated and ethene (CH₂=CH₂) is formed — this is compound C.

Part (a)(ii): Molecular mass of C (ethene, C₂H₄) = 2×12 + 4×1 = 24 + 4 = 28 u.

Part (a)(iii): When sodium carbonate is added to acetic acid (B), vigorous effervescence occurs due to release of CO₂ gas. The equation is: 2CH₃COOH + Na₂CO₃ → 2CH₃COONa + H₂O + CO₂↑.

Part (a)(iv): The electron dot structure of acetic acid (CH₃COOH) shows the methyl carbon bonded to 3 H atoms and to the carboxyl carbon; the carboxyl carbon has a double bond to one oxygen (C=O) and a single bond to another oxygen which has an H atom attached (O–H), with lone pairs on both oxygen atoms.

OR Part (b)(i): A homologous series is a series of carbon compounds in which successive members differ from each other by a –CH₂– group (14 u difference in molecular mass) and have the same functional group and similar chemical properties. For the –COOH (carboxylic acid) functional group: (1) Methanoic acid — HCOOH; (2) Ethanoic acid — CH₃COOH; (3) Propanoic acid — C₂H₅COOH.

Part (b)(ii): Two carbon compounds with carbon atoms in a ring structure are Benzene (C₆H₆) and Cyclohexane (C₆H₁₂). The structure of benzene shows a hexagonal ring of 6 carbon atoms with alternating single and double bonds, and each carbon bonded to one hydrogen atom.
questions.solution_hindi:
भाग (क)(i): A = इथेनॉल (C₂H₅OH); B = एसिटिक अम्ल (CH₃COOH, आण्विक द्रव्यमान 60u); C = इथीन (C₂H₄)।
(ii): C का आण्विक द्रव्यमान = 2×12 + 4×1 = 28 u।
(iii): 2CH₃COOH + Na₂CO₃ → 2CH₃COONa + H₂O + CO₂↑ (CO₂ बुलबुले के साथ निकलती है)।
(iv): CH₃COOH की इलेक्ट्रॉन-बिन्दु संरचना में C–H, C–C, C=O और O–H बंध तथा ऑक्सीजन पर एकाकी इलेक्ट्रॉन युग्म।
भाग (ख)(i): समजातीय श्रेणी में क्रमागत सदस्य –CH₂– से भिन्न होते हैं और समान कार्यात्मक समूह होता है। –COOH श्रेणी: मेथेनोइक अम्ल (HCOOH), एथेनोइक अम्ल (CH₃COOH), प्रोपेनोइक अम्ल (C₂H₅COOH)।
(ii): बेन्जीन (C₆H₆) और साइक्लोहेक्सेन (C₆H₁₂) में कार्बन वलय में व्यवस्थित हैं।

questions.text_english:
(a) (i) Write the functions of the following parts of human female reproductive system:
(I) Ovary
(II) Fallopian tube
(III) Uterus
(ii) State briefly two contraceptive methods used by human males.
OR
(b) (i) Differentiate between self-pollination and cross-pollination.
(ii) Identify A, B and C in the diagram given below and write one function of each.

key_points: (a)(i)(I) Ovary: produces eggs (ova) and female sex hormones (oestrogen and progesterone).
(a)(i)(II) Fallopian tube: carries the egg from the ovary to the uterus; fertilisation normally occurs here.
(a)(i)(III) Uterus: site of implantation and development of the embryo/foetus during pregnancy.
(a)(ii) Condom: a physical barrier that prevents sperm from entering the vagina. Vasectomy: surgical cutting or blocking of the vas deferens to prevent sperm from being released during ejaculation.

(b)(i) Self-pollination: transfer of pollen from anther to stigma of the same flower. Cross-pollination: transfer of pollen from anther of one flower to stigma of a different flower of the same species.

(b)(ii) A = Style (connects stigma to ovary; provides pathway for pollen tube); B = Ovule (contains the female gamete; develops into seed after fertilisation); C = Ovary (encloses ovule; develops into fruit after fertilisation).

questions.solution:
Part (a)(i): (I) Ovary — The ovaries are the primary female reproductive organs. They produce eggs (ova) through the process of oogenesis and also secrete female sex hormones, oestrogen and progesterone, which regulate the menstrual cycle and secondary sexual characteristics. (II) Fallopian Tube — The fallopian tube (oviduct) carries the released egg from the ovary towards the uterus. It is the site where fertilisation of the egg by a sperm normally takes place. The fertilised egg (zygote) then moves to the uterus. (III) Uterus — The uterus is a hollow, pear-shaped muscular organ where the fertilised egg implants and develops into an embryo and then a foetus. It nourishes the developing baby through the placenta and expels it at birth through muscular contractions.

Part (a)(ii): Two contraceptive methods used by males are: (1) Condom — A mechanical/physical barrier contraceptive that is worn over the penis during intercourse, preventing sperm from entering the female reproductive tract and thereby preventing fertilisation. It also protects against sexually transmitted diseases. (2) Vasectomy — A permanent surgical contraceptive method in which the vas deferens (sperm duct) is cut and tied, preventing sperm from being released during ejaculation.

OR Part (b)(i): Self-pollination is the transfer of pollen grains from the anther to the stigma of the same flower (or another flower on the same plant). It does not require a pollinating agent. Cross-pollination is the transfer of pollen grains from the anther of one flower to the stigma of a flower on a different plant of the same species. It requires pollinating agents like wind, water, or insects, and promotes genetic variation.

Part (b)(ii): In the diagram of a flower's pistil/ovule: A = Style — connects the stigma to the ovary; it provides the pathway through which the pollen tube grows down towards the ovule. B = Ovule — contains the female gamete (egg cell); after fertilisation it develops into a seed. C = Ovary — encloses and protects the ovule(s); after fertilisation it develops into a fruit.

sub_questions.text_english:
(i) What is the function of the earth wire? State the advantage of the earth wire in domestic electric appliances such as electric iron.
OR
(ii) List two precautions to be taken to avoid electrical accidents. State how these precautions prevent possible damage to the circuit/appliance.

key_points: (i) Earth wire provides a low resistance path to the ground for any leakage current. If the live wire accidentally touches the metallic body of an appliance like an electric iron, the excess current flows safely to earth through the earth wire instead of through the user's body, protecting from electric shock.

(ii) Precaution 1: Use a fuse/MCB in the circuit — if current exceeds safe limit, fuse melts and breaks the circuit, preventing overheating and fire. Precaution 2: Never touch live wires or faulty appliances with wet hands — water conducts electricity, so dry hands prevent accidental electrocution.

sub_questions.solution:
For part (i): The earth wire is a safety wire with green insulation that connects the metallic body of an electrical appliance to the ground (earth). Its function is to provide a low-resistance path for any leakage current to flow safely into the earth. In appliances like electric irons, if the live wire accidentally comes in contact with the metal body due to insulation failure, the leakage current flows through the earth wire to the ground instead of through the user's body. This prevents the user from receiving a potentially fatal electric shock and protects the appliance from damage.

For part (ii): Precaution 1 — Always use a fuse or Miniature Circuit Breaker (MCB) of appropriate rating in the circuit. If the current exceeds the safe limit due to a short circuit or overload, the fuse wire melts and breaks the circuit, preventing overheating of wires, damage to appliances, and the risk of fire. Precaution 2 — Never touch electrical wires, switches, or appliances with wet or damp hands. Water is a good conductor of electricity; touching live parts with wet hands can result in current passing through the body, causing electrocution.

key_points: Photosynthesis — the process by which green plants use sunlight, water and CO₂ to prepare food (glucose) in the presence of chlorophyll, releasing oxygen as a by-product.

sub_questions.solution: The process is Photosynthesis. It is defined as the process by which green plants (autotrophs) use carbon dioxide from the air and water from the soil, in the presence of sunlight and chlorophyll, to synthesise glucose (food) and release oxygen as a by-product.

sub_questions.solution: The balanced chemical equation for photosynthesis is: 6CO₂ + 6H₂O → (in the presence of sunlight and chlorophyll) → C₆H₁₂O₆ + 6O₂. Here, carbon dioxide and water are converted into glucose and oxygen using light energy.

sub_questions.text_english:
(i) State in proper sequence the events that occur in synthesis of food by desert plants.
OR
(ii) Explain giving reasons what happens to the rate at which the green plants will prepare food (I) during cloudy weather, and (II) when stomata get blocked due to dust.

key_points: (i) Desert plants (CAM plants): Night — stomata open, CO₂ absorbed and stored as organic acids (malic acid). Day — stomata remain closed to prevent water loss; stored CO₂ is released and used for photosynthesis using sunlight.

(ii)(I) During cloudy weather: rate of photosynthesis decreases because sunlight (light energy) is the primary requirement for the light reaction of photosynthesis; reduced light intensity slows down photosynthesis. (II) When stomata are blocked: CO₂ cannot enter the leaves, so the dark reaction (Calvin cycle) is severely affected, reducing the rate of photosynthesis significantly.

sub_questions.solution:
For part (i): Desert plants (called CAM — Crassulacean Acid Metabolism plants) have a special adaptation to conserve water. At night, their stomata open to allow CO₂ to enter the leaf, which is then fixed and stored as organic acids (like malic acid) in vacuoles. During the day, the stomata remain tightly closed to prevent water loss through transpiration. The stored organic acids release CO₂, which is then used along with sunlight and water to carry out the Calvin cycle (dark reaction) and synthesise glucose.

For part (ii): (I) During cloudy weather, the intensity of sunlight reaching the leaves is greatly reduced. Since light energy is essential for the light-dependent reactions of photosynthesis (for splitting water and producing ATP and NADPH), reduced light directly slows down these reactions, thereby decreasing the overall rate of photosynthesis. (II) When stomata get blocked by dust, CO₂ from the atmosphere cannot enter the leaf. Since CO₂ is the raw material for the Calvin cycle (dark reaction/CO₂ fixation), its shortage severely reduces the rate of food synthesis. Additionally, blocked stomata also reduce oxygen release and water vapour exchange.

sub_questions.solution: The electrolysis of brine (concentrated aqueous sodium chloride solution) produces three products. (i) A mild non-corrosive basic salt 'A', used for faster cooking, is strongly heated to produce a compound 'B', that is used for removing permanent hardness of water. Identify A and B and also write the equation for the reaction that occurs when A is heated.
OR
(ii) Define water of crystallisation. Give two examples of salts that have water of crystallisation.

key_points: (i) A = Baking soda (NaHCO₃, sodium hydrogen carbonate). B = Washing soda (Na₂CO₃, sodium carbonate). Equation: 2NaHCO₃ → (heat) → Na₂CO₃ + H₂O + CO₂.

(ii) Water of crystallisation is the fixed number of water molecules present in one formula unit of a salt crystal as an integral part of its crystalline structure. Examples: CuSO₄·5H₂O (blue vitriol) and FeSO₄·7H₂O (green vitriol).

sub_questions.solution:
For part (i): Salt A is Baking Soda (Sodium hydrogen carbonate, NaHCO₃). It is a mild, non-corrosive basic salt used in cooking as it releases CO₂ gas when heated, making food light and spongy. When baking soda is strongly heated, it decomposes to form compound B, which is Washing Soda (Sodium carbonate, Na₂CO₃). Washing soda is used to remove permanent hardness of water by precipitating calcium and magnesium ions. The equation is: 2NaHCO₃ → (heat) → Na₂CO₃ + H₂O + CO₂↑.

For part (ii): Water of crystallisation is defined as the fixed number of water molecules present in one formula unit of a salt that form an integral part of the crystalline structure of that salt. The water molecules are chemically bonded in a definite ratio to the salt and are responsible for the characteristic shape and colour of the crystals. Two examples of salts containing water of crystallisation are: (1) Copper sulphate pentahydrate — CuSO₄·5H₂O (blue vitriol), which contains 5 water molecules per formula unit and is blue in colour; (2) Ferrous sulphate heptahydrate — FeSO₄·7H₂O (green vitriol), which contains 7 water molecules per formula unit and is green in colour.
